import os
import sys
import subprocess

class TheForge:
    def __init__(self):
        self.project_name = "THE FORGE"
        self.version = "1.0.0"
        self.submodules = [
            "OpenSourceLudus", 
            "FRANKENSTINES-DEV-BOXX", 
            "injectioncgpt55", 
            "friendly-octo-invention"
        ]
        self.status = {}

    def initialize_system(self):
        print(f"--- INITIALIZING {self.project_name} ---")
        
        # 1. Check if all "Tools" are in the box
        for module in self.submodules:
            if os.path.exists(module):
                self.status[module] = "READY"
                print(f"[✔] {module} detected.")
            else:
                self.status[module] = "MISSING"
                print(f"[✘] WARNING: {module} not found.")

    def launch_brain(self):
        """Starts the AI Engine (OpenSourceLudus logic)"""
        print(f"\n--- WAKING THE BRAIN ---")
        if self.status["OpenSourceLudus"] == "READY":
            print("Injecting AI Copilot scripts into local runtime...")
            # Here, the script would trigger the LLM/Logic bridges
        else:
            print("Error: Brain (OpenSourceLudus) is missing.")

    def sync_engines(self, target="ALL"):
        """Pushes the Forge logic to Unity or Unreal"""
        print(f"\n--- SYNCING TO {target} ---")
        # Logic to copy the 'injectioncgpt' and 'octo' assets into Game Engine folders
        print(f"Propagating THE FORGE assets to Project Environments...")

    def boot_ui(self):
        """Launches the Forge Dashboard"""
        print(f"\n--- LAUNCHING THE FORGE DASHBOARD ---")
        print("Welcome, Architect. The world is ready for your command.")

# Run the system

    forge = TheForge()

public class ForgeBridge : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Path to the shared "Command Center" file where The Forge writes instructions
    private string commandFilePath;

    void Start()
    {
        // Points to a file in the Forge's shared directory
        commandFilePath = Path.Combine(Application.dataPath, "../../The_Injectors/live_command.txt");
        Debug.Log("[THE FORGE] Bridge Active. Listening for Architect commands...");

    {
        // Every frame, check if the Architect has sent a new command
        if (File.Exists(commandFilePath))
        {

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(command))
            {
                ExecuteForgeCommand(command);
                // Clear the command once executed so it doesn't run twice
                File.WriteAllText(commandFilePath, string.Empty);
            }
        }
    }

    void ExecuteForgeCommand(string cmd)
    {
        Debug.Log("[THE FORGE] Received Command: " + cmd);

        // Example Logic: If the AI tells the world to change
        if (cmd == "GRAVITY_FLIP") {
            Physics.gravity = new Vector3(0, 9.81f, 0);
        }
        else if (cmd == "SPAWN_WOLF") {
            // Your logic to spawn an NPC from The_Library
            Debug.Log("Spawning AI-driven NPC...");
        }
    }

generate the "Unity Bridge" C# script that allows Unity to 'listen' to the Forge's commands in real-time PLEASE AND THANK YOU

This is the "Nerve Center" for your game engine. To make THE FORGE actually control Unity, we need a bridge that doesn't just check the file every few seconds, but "listens" for changes instantly.

Below is the high-performance Unity Bridge script. It uses a File Watcher, which is like a motion sensor for your code—the moment your Python script writes a command, Unity feels it.

The Architecture of the Bridge
The Forge (Python): Writes a string (like DAY_NIGHT_TOGGLE) to a text file.

The Injector: The live_command.txt file acts as the shared mailbox.

The Bridge (Unity): This C# script "watches" the mailbox and executes the command on the next game frame.

The Script: ForgeBridge.cs
Create a new C# script in Unity named ForgeBridge.cs and paste this in:

C#
using UnityEngine;
using System.IO;
using System.Collections.Generic;

public class ForgeBridge : MonoBehaviour
{
    [Header("Forge Settings")]
    public string commandFileName = "live_command.txt";
    private string commandFilePath;

    // A thread-safe queue to store commands until Unity can run them
    private Queue<string> commandQueue = new Queue<string>();
    private FileSystemWatcher watcher;

    void Start()
    {
        // Path to the 'The_Injectors' folder in your THE-FORGE project
        commandFilePath = Path.Combine(Application.dataPath, "../../The_Injectors/");
        
        if (!Directory.Exists(commandFilePath)) {
            Directory.CreateDirectory(commandFilePath);
        }

        SetupWatcher();
        Debug.Log("<color=cyan>[THE FORGE]</color> Bridge Online. Listening at: " + commandFilePath);
    }

    void SetupWatcher()
    {
        watcher = new FileSystemWatcher();
        watcher.Path = commandFilePath;
        watcher.Filter = commandFileName;

        // Watch for when the file is updated or created
        watcher.NotifyFilter = NotifyFilters.LastWrite;
        watcher.Changed += OnForgeCommandReceived;
        watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = true;
    }

    private void OnForgeCommandReceived(object source, FileSystemEventArgs e)
    {
        // Read the file and put the command in the queue
        // We use a queue because Unity's API (moving objects, etc.) MUST happen on the Main Thread
        try {
            string cmd = File.ReadAllText(e.FullPath).Trim();
            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cmd)) {
                lock (commandQueue) {
                    commandQueue.Enqueue(cmd);
                }
            }
        } catch (IOException) {
            // Sometimes the file is locked while being written, we just skip that frame
        }
    }

    void Update()
    {
        // Process all commands that arrived since the last frame
        lock (commandQueue)
        {
            while (commandQueue.Count > 0)
            {
                string cmd = commandQueue.Dequeue();
                ExecuteCommand(cmd);
                // Clear the file after reading so it's ready for the next command
                File.WriteAllText(Path.Combine(commandFilePath, commandFileName), string.Empty);
            }
        }
    }

    void ExecuteCommand(string cmd)
    {
        Debug.Log("<color=green>[THE FORGE EXECUTE]:</color> " + cmd);

        // --- ADD YOUR CUSTOM COMMANDS HERE ---
        switch (cmd)
        {
            case "GRAVITY_UP":
                Physics.gravity = new Vector3(0, 20f, 0);
                break;
            case "GRAVITY_NORMAL":
                Physics.gravity = new Vector3(0, -9.81f, 0);
                break;
            case "SLOW_MO":
                Time.timeScale = 0.5f;
                break;
            case "NORMAL_TIME":
                Time.timeScale = 1.0f;
                break;
            default:
                Debug.LogWarning("Unknown Forge Command: " + cmd);
                break;
        }
    }

    void OnDestroy() {
        if (watcher != null) {
            watcher.EnableRaisingEvents = false;
            watcher.Dispose();
        }
    }
}
How to Use It (The 1-2-3 Step)
Drop it in: Create an empty GameObject in your Unity Scene called Forge_Controller and drag this script onto it.

The Connection: Ensure your THE-FORGE project folder is in the same main directory as your Unity Project folder. The script uses ../../ to step out of Unity and into your The_Injectors folder.

Test It: While Unity is in Play Mode, open the live_command.txt file in Notepad, type SLOW_MO, and hit Save. Your game will instantly slow down!

The Potential of this Bridge
Since you are using a Queue, you can send hundreds of commands per second. This means your Python AI could be controlling 50 different enemies, the weather, and the player's health all at once, without ever causing Unity to lag or crash.

1️⃣ ADoor ACTOR (AUTHORITATIVE, REPLICATED)

ADoor.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockStateChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ADoor : public AActor

{

GENERATED_BODY()



public:

ADoor();



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_Locked)

bool bIsLocked = false;



UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

FOnDoorLockStateChanged OnDoorLockStateChanged;



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void LockDoor();



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void UnlockDoor();



protected:

virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



UFUNCTION()

void OnRep_Locked();



void ApplyLockState();

};



ADoor.cpp

#include "Door.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ADoor::ADoor()

{

bReplicates = true;



DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>("DoorMesh");

RootComponent = DoorMesh;



DoorMesh->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

}



void ADoor::LockDoor()

{

if (!bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = true;

ApplyLockState();

}

}



void ADoor::UnlockDoor()

{

if (bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = false;

ApplyLockState();

}

}



void ADoor::ApplyLockState()

{

DoorMesh->SetCollisionEnabled(

bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics

: ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

);



OnDoorLockStateChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ADoor::OnRep_Locked()

{

ApplyLockState();

}



void ADoor::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(ADoor, bIsLocked);

}





This door:



Blocks movement when locked



Replicates cleanly



Broadcasts state changes for animation/UI



Requires no NavMesh rebuild



Collision blocking is enough. Keep it simple.

3️⃣ WIRE DOORS INTO LOCKDOWN (ScheduleManager or GameRules)



Add this to ScheduleManager.cpp (or GameRules if that’s your authority):



#include "Door.h"

#include "EngineUtils.h"



void AScheduleManager::StartLockdown()

{

bLockdownActive = true;



for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

{

It->LockDoor();

}

}

}



void AScheduleManager::EndLockdown()

{

bLockdownActive = false;



for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

{

It->UnlockDoor();

}

}

}

bIsRestrained = true

Holding cell



Seg intake point



Step 5: Segregation



Final step:



bInSegregation = true

Inmate sent to TP_SegCell



Timer or condition required to release

PART 1: Door Actor (C++ Backbone)

Create C++ class



Parent: AActor

Name: NH_Door



NH_Door.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "NH_Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_Door : public AActor

{

GENERATED_BODY()



public:

ANH_Door();



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UBoxComponent* Blocker;



UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly)

bool bIsLocked = false;



UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

FOnDoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void LockDoor();



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void UnlockDoor();



protected:

virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



UFUNCTION()

void OnRep_LockState();

};



NH_Door.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"

#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"

#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ANH_Door::ANH_Door()

{

bReplicates = true;



DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));

RootComponent = DoorMesh;



Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));

Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);

Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);

}



void ANH_Door::LockDoor()

{

if (!bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = true;

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics);

OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(true);

}

}



void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()

{

if (bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = false;

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);

OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(false);

}

}



void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()

{

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(

bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

);



OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);

}





What this does



Blocker physically blocks movement + NavMesh



No teleporting NPCs



No rebuilding nav every time



Works in PIE and multiplayer



PART 2: Hook Doors Into Lockdown



You already have GameRules / ScheduleManager. We extend it.



In ScheduleManager.h



Add:



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void SetLockdown(bool bEnable);



In ScheduleManager.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"



void AScheduleManager::SetLockdown(bool bEnable)

{

for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (bEnable)

{

It->LockDoor();

}

else

{

It->UnlockDoor();

}

}

}

🔧 FIX SET: INSTITUTIONAL GLUE (CANON)

1️⃣ InmateAuthorityComponent — SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE VIOLATIONS



Rule:



If a client guard reports a violation, it must RPC to the server.

The server is the only entity allowed to mutate institutional memory.



InmateAuthorityComponent.h (FIXED)

UFUNCTION(Server, Reliable)

void Server_RegisterViolation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context

);



void RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context

);



InmateAuthorityComponent.cpp (FIXED)

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::Server_RegisterViolation_Implementation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

FViolationRecord Record;

Record.Type = Type;

Record.Severity = Severity;

Record.ReportingGuard = ReportingGuard;

Record.Context = Context;

Record.GameTimeStamp = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();



ViolationHistory.Add(Record);

AuthorityLevel = FMath::Clamp(AuthorityLevel + Severity, 0, 5);

}



Usage rule (never break this):

if (GetOwner()->HasAuthority())

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(...);

}

else

{

Server_RegisterViolation(...);

}





That’s now network-correct and canonical.



2️⃣ InmateJudicialComponent — AUTOMATIC TICK VIA SCHEDULEMANAGER



Punishments do not self-tick.

They are ticked centrally by authority. This prevents desync and cheating.



InmateJudicialComponent.h (ADD)

void AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds);



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp (FIXED)

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

{

FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];

if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

{

ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

}

}

}





No timers.

No Tick() on inmates.

One clock. One authority.



3️⃣ Schedule ↔ Judicial INTEGRATION (NO GAPS)



Schedules must respect segregation every frame, not “on update.”



NH_ScheduleComponent.cpp (FIXED)

bool UNH_ScheduleComponent::IsScheduleOverriddenByJudicial() const

{

auto* Judicial = GetOwner()->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

return Judicial && Judicial->IsInSegregation();

}



In your schedule update logic:

if (IsScheduleOverriddenByJudicial())

{

ForceActivity("Segregation", "TP_SegCell");

return;

}





Schedules do not argue with court orders. Ever.



4️⃣ ScheduleManager — SINGLE AUTHORITY LOOP (THE SPINE)



This is where everything meets.



ScheduleManager.cpp (ADD TO TICK OR TIMER)

void AScheduleManager::AuthorityTick(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (TActorIterator<ACharacter> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

auto* Judicial = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

auto* Authority = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



if (Judicial)

{

Judicial->AdvanceJudicialTime(DeltaSeconds);

}



if (Authority)

{

Authority->DecayAuthority(DeltaSeconds);

}

}

}





Call this from:



GameState minute tick



Or a 1-second server timer



This is now the single integration point you demanded.

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

FViolationRecord Record;

Record.Type = Type;

Record.Severity = Severity;

Record.ReportingGuard = ReportingGuard;

Record.Context = Context;

Record.GameTimeStamp = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();



ViolationHistory.Add(Record);

AuthorityLevel = FMath::Clamp(AuthorityLevel + Severity, 0, 5);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, AuthorityLevel);

DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, ViolationHistory);

}

void AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds);



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

{

FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];



if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

{

ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

}

}

}





✅ No timers.

✅ No drift.

✅ One authority clock.

PHASE 5.1 — PAROLE ELIGIBILITY MODEL



Eligibility is computed, not granted.



Add to InmateJudicialComponent.h

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

bool IsEligibleForParole() const;



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp

bool UInmateJudicialComponent::IsEligibleForParole() const

{

float TotalServed = 0.f;

float TotalDuration = 0.f;



for (const FPunishmentRecord& P : ActivePunishments)

{

if (P.Duration < 0.f) return false; // Indefinite = no parole

TotalServed += P.TimeServed;

TotalDuration += P.Duration;

}



if (TotalDuration <= 0.f) return false;



const float ServedRatio = TotalServed / TotalDuration;

return ServedRatio >= 0.6f; // 60% served minimum (tunable)

}





Canon rules:



Indefinite segregation = no parole



Repeat offenders raise the threshold later



Faction hostility can invalidate eligibility (Phase 6)

void UParoleBoardComponent::EvaluateParole(ACharacter* Inmate)

{

auto* Judicial = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

auto* Authority = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



if (!Judicial || !Authority) return;



if (!Judicial->IsEligibleForParole())

{

DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("Sentence not sufficiently served"));

return;

}



if (Authority->AuthorityLevel >= 3)

{

DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("High institutional risk"));

return;

}



ApproveParole(Inmate, TEXT("Compliance satisfactory"));

}

+# Contributing to Auto Claude

+

+Thank you for your interest in contributing to Auto Claude! This document

+provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to the project.

+

+## Table of Contents

+

+- [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)

+- [Quick Start](#quick-start)

+- [Development Setup](#development-setup)

+ - [Python Backend](#python-backend)

+ - [Electron Frontend](#electron-frontend)

+- [Running from Source](#running-from-source)

+- [Pre-commit Hooks](#pre-commit-hooks)

+- [Code Style](#code-style)

+- [Testing](#testing)

+- [Continuous Integration](#continuous-integration)

+- [Git Workflow](#git-workflow)

+ - [Branch Overview](#branch-overview)

+ - [Main Branches](#main-branches)

+ - [Supporting Branches](#supporting-branches)

+ - [Branch Naming](#branch-naming)

+ - [Where to Branch From](#where-to-branch-from)

+ - [Pull Request Targets](#pull-request-targets)

+ - [Release Process (Maintainers)](#release-process-maintainers)

+ - [Commit Messages](#commit-messages)

+- [Pull Request Process](#pull-request-process)

+- [Issue Reporting](#issue-reporting)

+- [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)

+

+## Prerequisites

+

+Before contributing, ensure you have the following installed:

+

+- **Python 3.12+** - For the backend framework

+- **Node.js 24+** - For the Electron frontend

+- **npm 10+** - Package manager for the frontend (comes with Node.js)

+- **uv** (recommended) or **pip** - Python package manager

+- **Git** - Version control

+

+### Installing Python 3.12

+

+**Windows:**

+bash

+winget install Python.Python.3.12

+





+

+**macOS:**

+bash

+brew install python@3.12

+





+

+**Linux (Ubuntu/Debian):**

+bash

+sudo apt install python3.12 python3.12-venv

+





+

+## Quick Start

+

+The fastest way to get started:

+

+bash

+# Clone the repository

+git clone https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude.git

+cd Auto-Claude

+

+# Install all dependencies (cross-platform)

+npm run install:all

+

+# Run in development mode

+npm run dev

+

+# Or build and run production

+npm start

+



+

+## Development Setup

+

+The project consists of two main components:

+

+1. **Python Backend** (apps/backend/) - The core autonomous coding framework

+2. **Electron Frontend** (apps/frontend/) - Optional desktop UI

+

+### Python Backend

+

+The recommended way is to use npm run install:backend, but you can also

+set up manually:

+

+bash

+# Navigate to the backend directory

+cd apps/backend

+

+# Create virtual environment

+# Windows:

+py -3.12 -m venv .venv

+.venv\Scripts\activate

+

+# macOS/Linux:

+python3.12 -m venv .venv

+source .venv/bin/activate

+

+# Install dependencies

+pip install -r requirements.txt

+

+# Install test dependencies

+pip install -r ../../tests/requirements-test.txt

+

+# Set up environment

+cp .env.example .env

+# Edit .env and add your CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (get it via: claude setup-token)

+



+

+### Electron Frontend

+

+bash

+# Navigate to the frontend directory

+cd apps/frontend

+

+# Install dependencies

+npm install

+

+# Start development server

+npm run dev

+

+# Build for production

+npm run build

+

+# Package for distribution

+npm run package

+





+

+## Running from Source

+

+If you want to run Auto Claude from source (for development or testing

+unreleased features), follow these steps:

+

+### Step 1: Clone and Set Up

+

+bash

+git clone https://github.com/AndyMik90/Auto-Claude.git

+cd Auto-Claude/apps/backend

+

+# Using uv (recommended)

+uv venv && uv pip install -r requirements.txt

+

+# Or using standard Python

+python3 -m venv .venv

+source .venv/bin/activate # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate

+pip install -r requirements.txt

+

+# Set up environment

+cd apps/backend

+cp .env.example .env

+# Edit .env and add your CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (get it via: claude setup-token)

+



+

+### Step 2: Run the Desktop UI

+

+bash

+cd ../frontend

+

+# Install dependencies

+npm install

+

+# Development mode (hot reload)

+npm run dev

+

+# Or production build

+npm run build && npm run start

+





+

+## Pre-commit Hooks

+

+Install and run any configured hooks prior to opening a PR.

+

+## Code Style

+

+Follow existing project conventions and keep changes focused and readable.

+

+## Testing

+

+bash

+# Python (from repository root)

+npm run test:backend

+

+# Frontend

+cd apps/frontend && npm test && npm run lint && npm run typecheck

+





+

+## Continuous Integration

+

+CI runs the same checks as the testing commands above.

+

+## Git Workflow

+

+### Branch Overview

+

++main ─────●─────●─────●─────●───── (production)

+ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑

+develop ──●─────●─────●─────●───── (integration)

+ ↑ ↑ ↑

+feature/123 ────●

+feature/124 ──────────●

+hotfix/125 ─────────────────●───── (from main, merge to both)

+



+

+### Main Branches

+

+- main - production releases

+- develop - integration branch for upcoming releases

+

+### Supporting Branches

+

+- feature/* - new features (branch from develop)

+- hotfix/* - urgent production fixes (branch from main)

+

+### Branch Naming

+

+Use descriptive branch names:

+- feature/add-dark-mode

+- hotfix/150-critical-fix

+

+### Where to Branch From

+

+bash

+git checkout develop

+git pull origin develop

+git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name

+





+

+### Pull Request Targets

+

+- feature/* → develop

+- hotfix/* → main (then sync back to develop)

+

+### Release Process (Maintainers)

+

+See [RELEASE_PROCESS.md](RELEASE_PROCESS.md) for the full flow.

+

+### Commit Messages

+

+Write clear, concise commit messages that explain the **why** behind changes.

+

+**Format:**

++<type>: <subject>

+

+<body>

+

+<footer>

+





+

+- **type**: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore

+- **subject**: Short description (50 chars max, imperative mood)

+- **body**: Detailed explanation if needed (wrap at 72 chars)

+- **footer**: Reference issues, breaking changes

+

+**Examples:**

+bash

+# Good

+git commit -m "Add retry logic for failed API calls\n\nImplements exponential backoff for transient failures.\nFixes #123"

+

+# Avoid

+git commit -m "fix stuff"

+git commit -m "WIP"

+





+

+## Pull Request Process

+

+1. **Fork the repository** and create your branch from develop (not main!)

+2. **Make your changes** following the code style guidelines

+3. **Test thoroughly** (see [Testing](#testing))

+4. **Update documentation** if your changes affect:

+ - Public APIs

+ - Configuration options

+ - User-facing behavior

+5. **Create the Pull Request**:

+ - Use a clear, descriptive title

+ - Reference any related issues

+ - Describe what changes you made and why

+ - Include screenshots for UI changes

+ - List any breaking changes

+6. **PR Title Format**:

+ + <type>: <description>

+





+ Examples:

+ - feat: Add support for custom prompts

+ - fix: Resolve memory leak in worker process

+ - docs: Update installation instructions

+7. **Review Process**:

+ - Address reviewer feedback promptly

+ - Keep the PR focused on a single concern

+ - Squash commits if requested

+

+## Issue Reporting

+

+### Bug Reports

+

+When reporting a bug, include:

+

+1. **Clear title** describing the issue

+2. **Environment details**:

+ - OS and version

+ - Python version

+ - Node.js version (for UI issues)

+ - Auto Claude version

+3. **Steps to reproduce** the issue

+4. **Expected behavior** vs **actual behavior**

+5. **Error messages** or logs (if applicable)

+6. **Screenshots** (for UI issues)

+

+### Feature Requests

+

+When requesting a feature:

+

+1. **Describe the problem** you're trying to solve

+2. **Explain your proposed solution**

+3. **Consider alternatives** you've thought about

+4. **Provide context** on your use case

+

+## Architecture Overview

+

+Auto Claude consists of two main parts:

+

+### Python Backend (apps/backend/)

+

+The core autonomous coding framework:

+

+- **Entry Points**: run.py (build runner), spec_runner.py (spec creator)

+- **Agent System**: agent.py, client.py, prompts/

+- **Execution**: coordinator.py (parallel), worktree.py (isolation)

+- **Memory**: memory.py (file-based), graphiti_memory.py (graph-based)

+- **QA**: qa_loop.py, prompts/qa_*.md

+

+### Electron Frontend (apps/frontend/)

+

+Desktop interface:

+

+- **Main Process**: src/main/ - Electron main process, IPC handlers

+- **Renderer**: src/renderer/ - React UI components

+- **Shared**: src/shared/ - Types and utilities

+

+For detailed architecture information, see CLAUDE.md.

+# Release Process

+

+This document describes how releases are created for Auto Claude.

+

+## Versioning

+

+**Version Format:**

++X.Y.Z-beta.N (e.g., 2.8.0-beta.1, 2.8.0-beta.2)

+X.Y.Z-alpha.N (e.g., 2.8.0-alpha.1)

+X.Y.Z-rc.N (e.g., 2.8.0-rc.1)

+





+

+We follow Semantic Versioning:

+

+- **MAJOR (X.0.0):** Breaking changes, incompatible API changes

+- **MINOR (0.X.0):** New features, backwards compatible

+- **PATCH (0.0.X):** Bug fixes, backwards compatible

+

+## Beta Updates (User-Facing)

+

+Users can opt into beta updates in **Settings → Updates → “Beta Updates”**.

+When enabled, the app will check for and install beta versions. Users can

+switch back to stable at any time.

+

+## Release Flow

+

+Auto Claude uses an automated release pipeline that ensures releases are

+only published after all builds succeed.

+

++┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

+│ RELEASE FLOW │

+├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

+│ │

+│ develop branch main branch │

+│ ────────────── ─────────── │

+│ │ │ │

+│ │ 1. bump-version.js │ │

+│ │ (creates commit) │ │

+│ │ │ │

+│ ▼ │ │

+│ ┌─────────┐ │ │

+│ │ v2.8.0 │ 2. Create PR │ │

+│ │ commit │ ────────────────────► │ │

+│ └─────────┘ │ │

+│ │ │

+│ 3. Merge PR ▼ │

+│ ┌──────────┐ │

+│ │ v2.8.0 │ │

+│ │ on main │ │

+│ └────┬─────┘ │

+│ │ │

+│ ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐ │

+│ │ GitHub Actions (automatic) │ │

+│ ├───────────────────────────────────────┤ │

+│ │ 4. prepare-release.yml │ │

+│ │ - Detects version > latest tag │ │

+│ │ - Creates tag v2.8.0 │ │

+│ │ │ │

+│ │ 5. release.yml (triggered by tag) │ │

+│ │ - Builds macOS (Intel + ARM) │ │

+│ │ - Builds Windows │ │

+│ │ - Builds Linux │ │

+│ │ - Generates changelog │ │

+│ │ - Creates GitHub release │ │

+│ │ - Updates README │ │

+│ └───────────────────────────────────────┘ │

+│ │

+└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

+



+

+## For Maintainers: Creating a Release

+

+### Step 1: Bump the Version

+

+On your development branch (typically develop or a feature branch):

+

+bash

+# Navigate to project root

+cd /path/to/auto-claude

+

+# Bump version (choose one)

+node scripts/bump-version.js patch # 2.7.1 -> 2.7.2 (bug fixes)

+node scripts/bump-version.js minor # 2.7.1 -> 2.8.0 (new features)

+node scripts/bump-version.js major # 2.7.1 -> 3.0.0 (breaking changes)

+node scripts/bump-version.js 2.8.0 # Set specific version

+



+

+This will:

+

+- Update apps/frontend/package.json

+- Update package.json (root)

+- Update apps/backend/__init__.py

+- Create a commit with message chore: bump version to X.Y.Z

+

+### Step 2: Push and Create PR

+

+bash

+# Push your branch

+git push origin your-branch

+

+# Create PR to main (via GitHub UI or gh CLI)

+gh pr create --base main --title "Release v2.8.0"

+





+

+### Step 3: Merge to Main

+

+Once the PR is approved and merged to main, GitHub Actions will automatically:

+

+- Detect the version bump (prepare-release.yml)

+- Create a git tag (e.g., v2.8.0)

+- Trigger the release workflow (release.yml)

+- Build binaries for all platforms

+- Generate changelog from merged PRs (using release-drafter)

+- Scan binaries with VirusTotal

+- Create GitHub release with all artifacts

+- Update README with new version badge and download links

+

+### Step 4: Verify

+

+After merging, check:

+

+- GitHub Actions - ensure all workflows pass

+- Releases - verify release was created

+- README - confirm version updated

+

+## Hotfix Workflow

+

+For urgent production fixes that can’t wait for the normal release cycle:

+

+### 1. Create hotfix from main

+

+bash

+git checkout main

+git pull origin main

+git checkout -b hotfix/150-critical-fix

+





+

+### 2. Fix the issue

+

+bash

+# ... make changes ...

+git commit -m "hotfix: fix critical crash on startup"

+





+

+### 3. Open PR to main (fast-track review)

+

+bash

+gh pr create --base main --title "hotfix: fix critical crash on startup"

+





+

+### 4. After merge to main, sync to develop

+

+bash

+git checkout develop

+git pull origin develop

+git merge main

+git push origin develop

+



+

+> **Note:** Hotfixes branch FROM main and merge TO main first, then

+> sync back to develop to keep branches aligned.

+

+## Changelog Generation

+

+Changelogs are automatically generated from merged PRs using Release Drafter.

+

+### PR Labels for Changelog Categories

+

+| Label(s) | Category |

+|---------|----------|

+| feature, enhancement | New Features |

+| bug, fix | Bug Fixes |

+| improvement, refactor | Improvements |

+| documentation | Documentation |

+| (any other) | Other Changes |

+

+## Workflows

+

+| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |

+|---------|---------|---------|

+| prepare-release.yml | Push to main | Detects version bump, creates tag |

+| release.yml | Tag v* pushed | Builds binaries, creates release |

+| validate-version.yml | Tag v* pushed | Validates tag matches package.json |

+| update-readme (in release.yml) | After release | Updates README with new version |

+

+## Troubleshooting

+

+### Release didn't trigger after merge

+

+Check if version in package.json is greater than latest tag:

+

+bash

+git tag -l 'v*' --sort=-version:refname | head -1

+cat apps/frontend/package.json | grep version

+



+

+Ensure the merge commit touched package.json:

+

+bash

+git diff HEAD~1 --name-only | grep package.json

+





+

+### Build failed after tag was created

+

+- The release won't be published if builds fail.

+- Fix the issue and create a new patch version.

+- Don't reuse failed version numbers.

+

+### README shows wrong version

+

+README is only updated after successful release. If release failed, README

+keeps the previous version (this is intentional).

+

+## Manual Release (Emergency Only)

+

+In rare cases where you need to bypass the automated flow:

+

+bash

+git tag -a v2.8.0 -m "Release v2.8.0"

+git push origin v2.8.0

+





+

+> **Warning:** Only do this if you're certain the version in package.json

+> matches the tag.

+

+## Security

+

+All releases are:

+

+- Scanned with VirusTotal before publishing

+- Include SHA256 checksums for verification

+- Code-signed where applicable (macOS)

1️⃣ ADoor ACTOR (AUTHORITATIVE, REPLICATED)

ADoor.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockStateChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ADoor : public AActor

{

GENERATED_BODY()



public:

ADoor();



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, BlueprintReadOnly, ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_Locked)

bool bIsLocked = false;



UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

FOnDoorLockStateChanged OnDoorLockStateChanged;



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void LockDoor();



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void UnlockDoor();



protected:

virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



UFUNCTION()

void OnRep_Locked();



void ApplyLockState();

};



ADoor.cpp

#include "Door.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ADoor::ADoor()

{

bReplicates = true;



DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>("DoorMesh");

RootComponent = DoorMesh;



DoorMesh->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

}



void ADoor::LockDoor()

{

if (!bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = true;

ApplyLockState();

}

}



void ADoor::UnlockDoor()

{

if (bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = false;

ApplyLockState();

}

}



void ADoor::ApplyLockState()

{

DoorMesh->SetCollisionEnabled(

bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics

: ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

);



OnDoorLockStateChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ADoor::OnRep_Locked()

{

ApplyLockState();

}



void ADoor::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(ADoor, bIsLocked);

}





This door:



Blocks movement when locked



Replicates cleanly



Broadcasts state changes for animation/UI



Requires no NavMesh rebuild



Collision blocking is enough. Keep it simple.

3️⃣ WIRE DOORS INTO LOCKDOWN (ScheduleManager or GameRules)



Add this to ScheduleManager.cpp (or GameRules if that’s your authority):



#include "Door.h"

#include "EngineUtils.h"



void AScheduleManager::StartLockdown()

{

bLockdownActive = true;



for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

{

It->LockDoor();

}

}

}



void AScheduleManager::EndLockdown()

{

bLockdownActive = false;



for (TActorIterator<ADoor> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (It->ActorHasTag("LockdownDoor"))

{

It->UnlockDoor();

}

}

}





That’s it. No drama.

ESCALATION FLOW (THIS IS THE RULESET)

Step 1: Detection



A guard detects a violation when:



Inmate is not at scheduled TargetPoint



Inmate tries to pass a locked door



Inmate is in a restricted area during lockdown



Detection can be:



Simple overlap check



Line of sight



Schedule mismatch



No perception wizardry yet.



Step 2: Warning



Guard approaches inmate and issues warning.



Effects:



Inmate CurrentViolationLevel = 1



Guard sets a short timer (10–30 seconds)



UI / debug text shows “Warning issued”



If inmate complies:



Violation resets to 0



Guard disengages



Step 3: Intervention



If inmate ignores warning:



Guard blocks path



Forces inmate schedule override to GuardTarget



CurrentViolationLevel = 2



Inmate movement is constrained but not restrained.



Step 4: Restraint



If inmate resists or keeps violating:



bIsRestrained = true



Movement speed = near zero



Guard escorts inmate to:



Holding cell



Seg intake point



Step 5: Segregation



Final step:



bInSegregation = true



Schedule overridden permanently (for now)



Inmate sent to TP_SegCell



Timer or condition required to release



That’s punishment. Clear. Predictable. Systemic.

PART 1: Door Actor (C++ Backbone)

Create C++ class



Parent: AActor

Name: NH_Door



NH_Door.h

#pragma once



#include "CoreMinimal.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"

#include "NH_Door.generated.h"



DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE_OneParam(FOnDoorLockChanged, bool, bLocked);



UCLASS()

class NYGHTSHADEHOLLOW_API ANH_Door : public AActor

{

GENERATED_BODY()



public:

ANH_Door();



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UStaticMeshComponent* DoorMesh;



UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere)

UBoxComponent* Blocker;



UPROPERTY(ReplicatedUsing=OnRep_LockState, BlueprintReadOnly)

bool bIsLocked = false;



UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable)

FOnDoorLockChanged OnDoorLockChanged;



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void LockDoor();



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void UnlockDoor();



protected:

virtual void GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const override;



UFUNCTION()

void OnRep_LockState();

};



NH_Door.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"

#include "Components/StaticMeshComponent.h"

#include "Components/BoxComponent.h"

#include "Net/UnrealNetwork.h"



ANH_Door::ANH_Door()

{

bReplicates = true;



DoorMesh = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(TEXT("DoorMesh"));

RootComponent = DoorMesh;



Blocker = CreateDefaultSubobject<UBoxComponent>(TEXT("Blocker"));

Blocker->SetupAttachment(RootComponent);

Blocker->SetCollisionProfileName("BlockAll");

Blocker->SetHiddenInGame(true);

}



void ANH_Door::LockDoor()

{

if (!bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = true;

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics);

OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(true);

}

}



void ANH_Door::UnlockDoor()

{

if (bIsLocked)

{

bIsLocked = false;

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision);

OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(false);

}

}



void ANH_Door::OnRep_LockState()

{

Blocker->SetCollisionEnabled(

bIsLocked ? ECollisionEnabled::QueryAndPhysics : ECollisionEnabled::NoCollision

);



OnDoorLockChanged.Broadcast(bIsLocked);

}



void ANH_Door::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(ANH_Door, bIsLocked);

}





What this does



Blocker physically blocks movement + NavMesh



No teleporting NPCs



No rebuilding nav every time



Works in PIE and multiplayer



PART 2: Hook Doors Into Lockdown



You already have GameRules / ScheduleManager. We extend it.



In ScheduleManager.h



Add:



UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

void SetLockdown(bool bEnable);



In ScheduleManager.cpp

#include "NH_Door.h"



void AScheduleManager::SetLockdown(bool bEnable)

{

for (TActorIterator<ANH_Door> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

if (bEnable)

{

It->LockDoor();

}

else

{

It->UnlockDoor();

}

}

}





Now when lockdown triggers, doors respond globally.

1️⃣ InmateAuthorityComponent — SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE VIOLATIONS

void Server_RegisterViolation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

const FString& Context

);



void RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

);



InmateAuthorityComponent.cpp (FIXED)

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::Server_RegisterViolation_Implementation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

FViolationRecord Record;

Record.Type = Type;

Record.Severity = Severity;

Record.ReportingGuard = ReportingGuard;

Record.Context = Context;

Record.GameTimeStamp = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();



ViolationHistory.Add(Record);

AuthorityLevel = FMath::Clamp(AuthorityLevel + Severity, 0, 5);

}



Usage rule (never break this):

if (GetOwner()->HasAuthority())

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(...);

}

else

{

Server_RegisterViolation(...);

}





That’s now network-correct and canonical.



2️⃣ InmateJudicialComponent — AUTOMATIC TICK VIA SCHEDULEMANAGER



Punishments do not self-tick.

They are ticked centrally by authority. This prevents desync and cheating.



InmateJudicialComponent.h (ADD)

void AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds);



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp (FIXED)

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

{

FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];

if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

{

ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

}

}

}





No timers.

No Tick() on inmates.

One clock. One authority.

NH_ScheduleComponent.cpp (FIXED)

bool UNH_ScheduleComponent::IsScheduleOverriddenByJudicial() const

{

auto* Judicial = GetOwner()->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

return Judicial && Judicial->IsInSegregation();

}



In your schedule update logic:

if (IsScheduleOverriddenByJudicial())

{

ForceActivity("Segregation", "TP_SegCell");

Schedules do not argue with court orders. Ever.



4️⃣ ScheduleManager — SINGLE AUTHORITY LOOP (THE SPINE)



This is where everything meets.



ScheduleManager.cpp (ADD TO TICK OR TIMER)

void AScheduleManager::AuthorityTick(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (TActorIterator<ACharacter> It(GetWorld()); It; ++It)

{

auto* Judicial = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

auto* Authority = It->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



if (Judicial)

{

Judicial->AdvanceJudicialTime(DeltaSeconds);

}



if (Authority)

{

Authority->DecayAuthority(DeltaSeconds);

}

}

}





Call this from:



GameState minute tick



Or a 1-second server timer



This is now the single integration point you demanded.

void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

if (GetOwner()->HasAuthority())

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}

else

{

Server_RegisterViolation(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::Server_RegisterViolation_Implementation(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

RegisterViolation_Internal(Type, Severity, ReportingGuard, Context);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::RegisterViolation_Internal(

EViolationType Type,

int32 Severity,

FName ReportingGuard,

const FString& Context)

{

FViolationRecord Record;

Record.Type = Type;

Record.Severity = Severity;

Record.ReportingGuard = ReportingGuard;

Record.Context = Context;

Record.GameTimeStamp = GetWorld()->GetTimeSeconds();



ViolationHistory.Add(Record);

AuthorityLevel = FMath::Clamp(AuthorityLevel + Severity, 0, 5);

}



void UInmateAuthorityComponent::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(

TArray<FLifetimeProperty>& OutLifetimeProps) const

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(OutLifetimeProps);

DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, AuthorityLevel);

DOREPLIFETIME(UInmateAuthorityComponent, ViolationHistory);

}

InmateJudicialComponent.cpp

void UInmateJudicialComponent::AdvanceJudicialTime(float DeltaSeconds)

{

for (int32 i = ActivePunishments.Num() - 1; i >= 0; --i)

{

FPunishmentRecord& P = ActivePunishments[i];



if (P.Duration < 0.f) continue;



P.TimeServed += DeltaSeconds;



if (P.TimeServed >= P.Duration)

{

ActivePunishments.RemoveAt(i);

}

}

}





✅ No timers.

✅ No drift.

✅ One authority clock.

PHASE 5.1 — PAROLE ELIGIBILITY MODEL



Eligibility is computed, not granted.



Add to InmateJudicialComponent.h

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable)

bool IsEligibleForParole() const;



InmateJudicialComponent.cpp

bool UInmateJudicialComponent::IsEligibleForParole() const

{

float TotalServed = 0.f;

float TotalDuration = 0.f;



for (const FPunishmentRecord& P : ActivePunishments)

{

if (P.Duration < 0.f) return false; // Indefinite = no parole

TotalServed += P.TimeServed;

TotalDuration += P.Duration;

}



if (TotalDuration <= 0.f) return false;



const float ServedRatio = TotalServed / TotalDuration;

return ServedRatio >= 0.6f; // 60% served minimum (tunable)

}





Canon rules:



Indefinite segregation = no parole



Repeat offenders raise the threshold later



Faction hostility can invalidate eligibility (Phase 6)

void UParoleBoardComponent::EvaluateParole(ACharacter* Inmate)

{

auto* Judicial = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>();

auto* Authority = Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateAuthorityComponent>();



if (!Judicial || !Authority) return;



if (!Judicial->IsEligibleForParole())

{

DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("Sentence not sufficiently served"));

return;

}



if (Authority->AuthorityLevel >= 3)

{

DenyParole(Inmate, TEXT("High institutional risk"));

return;

}



ApproveParole(Inmate, TEXT("Compliance satisfactory"));

}



void UParoleBoardComponent::ApproveParole(ACharacter* Inmate, const FString& Reason)

{

UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Parole approved for %s: %s"),

*Inmate->GetName(), *Reason);



// Phase 6 hook: faction response

Inmate->FindComponentByClass<UInmateJudicialComponent>()

->ActivePunishments.Empty();

}



void UParoleBoardComponent::DenyParole(ACharacter* Inmate, const FString& Reason)

{

UE_LOG(LogTemp, Warning, TEXT("Parole denied for %s: %s"),

*Inmate->GetName(), *Reason);



// Extend sentence slightly

}

float UFactionReputationComponent::GetReputation(EFaction Faction) const

{

{

return *Value;

}

return 0.f;

}



void UFactionReputationComponent::ModifyReputation(EFaction Faction, float Delta)

{

Reputation.FindOrAdd(Faction) =

FMath::Clamp(GetReputation(Faction) + Delta, -100.f, 100.f);

}

{

Super::GetLifetimeReplicatedProps(Out);

DOREPLIFETIME(UFactionReputationComponent, Reputation);

}

PS C:\Windows\System32> function Score-UProject {

>> param([string]$UProjectPath)

>> $dir = Split-Path -Parent $UProjectPath

>>

>> $hasSource = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Source")

>> $hasContent = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Content")

>> $hasConfig = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Config")

>> $isTemplate = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Templates\*"

>> $isEngine = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Engine\*"

>>

>> $sourceCount = 0

>> $contentCount = 0

>> if ($hasSource) { $sourceCount = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Source") -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }

>> if ($hasContent) { $contentCount = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Content") -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }

>>

>> # Heuristic scoring:

>> # - Prefer real projects over templates/engine programs

>> # - Prefer having Source/Content/Config

>> # - Prefer more content + some source

>> $score = 0

>> if ($hasContent) { $score += 200 }

>> if ($hasConfig) { $score += 50 }

>> if ($hasSource) { $score += 120 }

>> if ($contentCount -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(400, [int]([Math]::Log10($contentCount + 1) * 200)) }

>> if ($sourceCount -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(250, [int]([Math]::Log10($sourceCount + 1) * 150)) }

>>

>> if ($isTemplate) { $score -= 1000 }

>> if ($isEngine) { $score -= 800 }

>>

>> # Prefer things under the workspace root

>> if ($UProjectPath.StartsWith($WorkspaceRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {

>> $score += 250

>> }

>>

>> [pscustomobject]@{

>> UProject = $UProjectPath

>> ProjectDir = $dir

>> Score = $score

>> HasSource = $hasSource

>> HasContent = $hasContent

>> HasConfig = $hasConfig

>> SourceCount = $sourceCount

>> ContentCount = $contentCount

>> IsTemplate = $isTemplate

>> IsEngine = $isEngine

>> }

>> }

>>

>> if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $full) -and -not $Force) {

>> Write-Host "SKIP (exists): $Path (use -Force to overwrite)" -ForegroundColor Yellow

>> return

>> }

>>

>> $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)

>> [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($full, $Content, $utf8NoBom)

>> Write-Host "WROTE: $Path" -ForegroundColor Green

>> }

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_foreman_audit.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_foreman_audit = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$WorkspaceRoot,

>>

>> [string[]]$Roots = @(

>> "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop",

>> "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\Unreal Projects",

>> "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\ltvall",

>> "D:\",

>> "C:\"

>> ),

>>

>> [string]$OutCsv = (Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "Desktop\NH_UPROJECT_AUDIT.csv"),

>>

>> [switch]$PickBest

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> function Score-UProject {

>> param([string]$UProjectPath)

>> $dir = Split-Path -Parent $UProjectPath

>>

>> $hasSource = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Source")

>> $hasContent = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Content")

>> $hasConfig = Test-Path (Join-Path $dir "Config")

>> $isTemplate = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Templates\*"

>> $isEngine = $UProjectPath -like "*\Program Files\Epic Games\*\Engine\*"

>>

>> $sourceCount = 0

>> $contentCount = 0

>> if ($hasSource) { $sourceCount = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Source") -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }

>> if ($hasContent) { $contentCount = (Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $dir "Content") -Recurse -File -EA SilentlyContinue | Measure-Object).Count }

>>

>> # Heuristic scoring:

>> # - Prefer real projects over templates/engine programs

>> # - Prefer having Source/Content/Config

>> # - Prefer more content + some source

>> $score = 0

>> if ($hasContent) { $score += 200 }

>> if ($hasConfig) { $score += 50 }

>> if ($hasSource) { $score += 120 }

>> if ($contentCount -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(400, [int]([Math]::Log10($contentCount + 1) * 200)) }

>> if ($sourceCount -gt 0) { $score += [Math]::Min(250, [int]([Math]::Log10($sourceCount + 1) * 150)) }

>>

>> if ($isTemplate) { $score -= 1000 }

>> if ($isEngine) { $score -= 800 }

>>

>> # Prefer things under the workspace root

>> if ($UProjectPath.StartsWith($WorkspaceRoot, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {

>> $score += 250

>> }

>>

>> [pscustomobject]@{

>> UProject = $UProjectPath

>> ProjectDir = $dir

>> Score = $score

>> HasSource = $hasSource

>> HasContent = $hasContent

>> HasConfig = $hasConfig

>> SourceCount = $sourceCount

>> ContentCount = $contentCount

>> IsTemplate = $isTemplate

>> IsEngine = $isEngine

>> }

>> }

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $WorkspaceRoot)) {

>> throw "WorkspaceRoot not found: $WorkspaceRoot"

>> }

>>

>> $scanRoots = @($WorkspaceRoot) + ($Roots | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path $_) } | Select-Object -Unique)

>>

>> Write-Host "=== Foreman Audit ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> Write-Host "WorkspaceRoot: $WorkspaceRoot"

>> Write-Host "Scan roots:"; $scanRoots | ForEach-Object { Write-Host " - $_" }

>>

>> $uprojects = foreach ($r in $scanRoots) {

>> Get-ChildItem -Path $r -Filter *.uproject -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>> }

>>

>> if (!$uprojects) {

>> Write-Host "No .uproject files found." -ForegroundColor Red

>> exit 2

>> }

>>

>> $report = $uprojects | ForEach-Object { Score-UProject $_.FullName } | Sort-Object Score -Descending

>>

>> $report | Export-Csv -NoTypeInformation -Path $OutCsv

>> Write-Host "Wrote CSV: $OutCsv" -ForegroundColor Green

>>

>> $top = $report | Select-Object -First 10

>> Write-Host "nTop candidates:" -ForegroundColor Cyan>> $top |if ($PickBest) {

>> $best = $report | Select-Object -First 1

>> Write-Host "nBEST:" -ForegroundColor Green>> $best | Format-List

>> # Print only the path last (easy copy)

>> Write-Output $best.UProject

>> }

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_clean_project.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_clean_project = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$ProjectDir,

>>

>> [switch]$NukeDerivedDataCache,

>> [switch]$AlsoGlobalDDC

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> function Zap([string]$p) {

>> if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($p)) { return }

>> if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p) {

>> Write-Host "Deleting: $p" -ForegroundColor Yellow

>> Remove-Item -LiteralPath $p -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>> }

>> }

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir)) {

>> throw "ProjectDir not found: $ProjectDir"

>> }

>>

>> # Kill Unreal Editor if running

>> Get-Process UnrealEditor -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>>

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Binaries")

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Intermediate")

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "Saved")

>>

>> if ($NukeDerivedDataCache) {

>> Zap (Join-Path $ProjectDir "DerivedDataCache")

>> }

>>

>> if ($AlsoGlobalDDC) {

>> $globalDDC = Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA "UnrealEngine\Common\DerivedDataCache"

>> Zap $globalDDC

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host "✅ Cleanup done." -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_copy_uassets.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_copy_uassets = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$VaultPath,

>>

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$ProjectDir,

>>

>> [string]$DestSubdir = "PrisonCore",

>>

>> [switch]$UseRobocopy

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $VaultPath)) { throw "VaultPath not found: $VaultPath" }

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ProjectDir)) { throw "ProjectDir not found: $ProjectDir" }

>>

>> $dest = Join-Path $ProjectDir "Content\$DestSubdir"

>> New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dest | Out-Null

>>

>> Write-Host "Copying .uasset/.umap from:" -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> Write-Host " Vault: $VaultPath"

>> Write-Host " Dest : $dest"

>>

>> # If robocopy requested and available, use it (faster + preserves structure cleanly)

>> if ($UseRobocopy -and (Get-Command robocopy.exe -EA SilentlyContinue)) {

>> $args = @(

>> ""$VaultPath"",

>> ""$dest"",

>> "*.uasset",

>> "*.umap",

>> "/E",

>> "/R:1",

>> "/W:1",

>> "/NFL","/NDL","/NJH","/NJS","/NP"

>> )

>> & robocopy @args | Out-Host

>> Write-Host "✅ Robocopy pass complete." -ForegroundColor Green

>> exit 0

>> }

>>

>> # Pure PowerShell copy (slower but works everywhere)

>> $items = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $VaultPath -Recurse -Force -File -EA SilentlyContinue |

>> Where-Object { $_.Extension -in ".uasset",".umap" }

>>

>> if (!$items) {

>> Write-Host "No .uasset/.umap files found in vault." -ForegroundColor Yellow

>> exit 0

>> }

>>

>> foreach ($it in $items) {

>> $rel = $it.FullName.Substring($VaultPath.Length).TrimStart('\','/')

>> $target = Join-Path $dest $rel

>> $targetDir = Split-Path -Parent $target

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $targetDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $targetDir | Out-Null }

>> Copy-Item -LiteralPath $it.FullName -Destination $target -Force

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host ("✅ Copied {0} assets." -f $items.Count) -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_build_safe.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_build_safe = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$UProjectPath,

>>

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$UE57Root,

>>

>> [ValidateSet("Win64")]

>> [string]$Platform = "Win64",

>>

>> [ValidateSet("Development","DebugGame","Shipping")]

>> [string]$Config = "Development",

>>

>> [int]$MaxParallelActions = 6,

>>

>> [switch]$RegenerateProjectFiles

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $UProjectPath)) { throw "UProjectPath not found: $UProjectPath" }

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $UE57Root)) { throw "UE57Root not found: $UE57Root" }

>>

>> $buildBat = Join-Path $UE57Root "Engine\Build\BatchFiles\Build.bat"

>> $gpfBat = Join-Path $UE57Root "Engine\Build\BatchFiles\GenerateProjectFiles.bat"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $buildBat)) { throw "Build.bat not found: $buildBat" }

>>

>> $projName = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($UProjectPath)

>> $target = "${projName}Editor"

>>

>> # Kill any editor leftovers

>> Get-Process UnrealEditor -EA SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -EA SilentlyContinue

>>

>> if ($RegenerateProjectFiles) {

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $gpfBat)) { throw "GenerateProjectFiles.bat not found: $gpfBat" }

>> Write-Host "Regenerating project files..." -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> & $gpfBat "-Project=$UProjectPath" -Game -Engine | Out-Host

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host "Building $target ($Platform/$Config) MaxParallelActions=$MaxParallelActions" -ForegroundColor Cyan

>> & $buildBat $target $Platform $Config "-Project=$UProjectPath" -WaitMutex "-MaxParallelActions=$MaxParallelActions" | Out-Host

>>

>> Write-Host "✅ Build finished." -ForegroundColor Green

>> '@

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Tools\nh_git_init_ue.ps1

>> # ---------------------------

>> $nh_git_init_ue = @'

>> [CmdletBinding()]

>> param(

>> [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)]

>> [string]$RepoRoot,

>>

>> [string]$RemoteUrl = "",

>>

>> [string]$DefaultBranch = "main"

>> )

>>

>> Set-StrictMode -Version Latest

>> $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

>>

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $RepoRoot)) { throw "RepoRoot not found: $RepoRoot" }

>>

>> function Run([string]$cmd) {

>> Write-Host ">> $cmd" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

>> cmd.exe /c $cmd

>> if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Command failed: $cmd" }

>> }

>>

>> Push-Location $RepoRoot

>> try {

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $RepoRoot ".git"))) {

>> Run "git init"

>> }

>>

>> # Ensure branch name

>> Run "git checkout -B $DefaultBranch"

>>

>> # LFS

>> Run "git lfs install"

>>

>> # .gitattributes for UE assets

>> $ga = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitattributes"

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $ga)) {

>> @"

>> *.uasset filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.umap filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.fbx filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.png filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.tga filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> *.wav filter=lfs diff=lfs merge=lfs -text

>> "@ | Set-Content -Path $ga -Encoding utf8

>> }

>>

>> # .gitignore (standard UE)

>> $gi = Join-Path $RepoRoot ".gitignore"

>> if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $gi)) {

>> @"

>> # Unreal Engine

>> Binaries/

>> DerivedDataCache/

>> Intermediate/

>> Saved/

>> .vscode/

>> .vs/

>> *.sln

>> *.opensdf

>> *.sdf

>> *.suo

>> *.user

>> *.userprefs

>> *.VC.db

>> *.VC.VC.opendb

>> *.pdb

>> *.log

>>

>> # Build artifacts

>> Build/

>> "@ | Set-Content -Path $gi -Encoding utf8

>> }

>>

>> Run "git add .gitattributes .gitignore"

>> Run "git add -A"

>> Run "git commit -m "Initialize UE repo + LFS tracking""

>>

>> if ($RemoteUrl -and $RemoteUrl.Trim().Length -gt 0) {

>> $existing = (git remote) 2>$null

>> if ($existing -notcontains "origin") {

>> Run "git remote add origin $RemoteUrl"

>> } else {

>> Run "git remote set-url origin $RemoteUrl"

>> }

>> Run "git push -u origin $DefaultBranch"

>> }

>>

>> Write-Host "✅ Git init complete." -ForegroundColor Green

>> }

>> finally {

>> Pop-Location

>> }

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Content\Python\vault_to_unreal.py

>> # ---------------------------

>> $vault_to_unreal = @'

>> # vault_to_unreal.py

>> # Run INSIDE Unreal Editor (Python enabled) or via:

>> # UnrealEditor.exe "Path\Project.uproject" -ExecutePythonScript="...\Content\Python\vault_to_unreal.py"

>> #

>> # What it does:

>> # - Imports FBX + PNG from a vault folder into /Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets

>> # - Creates simple master materials (BaseColor + Normal)

>> # - Creates material instances per mesh and assigns best-guess textures

>> # - Assigns MI to static meshes

>> # - Fixes up redirectors

>>

>> import os

>> import re

>> import unreal

>>

>> # ------------------------

>> # CONFIG

>> # ------------------------

>> VAULT_ROOT = r"C:\Nyghtshade_Assets_Vault"

>> DEST_ROOT = "/Game/Nyghtshade/Final_Prison_Assets"

>>

>> TEXTURES_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Textures"

>> MESHES_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Meshes"

>> MATS_DIR = f"{DEST_ROOT}/Materials"

>>

>> CONCRETE_HINTS = ("concrete", "cement", "wall", "floor", "stone")

>> METAL_HINTS = ("metal", "steel", "iron", "pipe", "grate", "bar")

>>

>> # ------------------------

>> # HELPERS

>> # ------------------------

>> def log(msg: str):

>> unreal.log(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def warn(msg: str):

>> unreal.log_warning(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def err(msg: str):

>> unreal.log_error(f"[Foreman] {msg}")

>>

>> def ensure_dir(path: str):

>> if not unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_directory_exist(path):

>> unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.make_directory(path)

>>

>> def safe_asset_name(s: str) -> str:

>> s = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_]+", "_", s)

>> s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s).strip("_")

>> if not s:

>> s = "Asset"

>> return s[:120]

>>

>> def find_files(root: str, exts: set):

>> out = []

>> for base, _, files in os.walk(root):

>> for f in files:

>> ext = os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower()

>> if ext in exts:

>> out.append(os.path.join(base, f))

>> return out

>>

>> def import_file(src_path: str, dest_path: str, automated=True, replace=True):

>> task = unreal.AssetImportTask()

>> task.filename = src_path

>> task.destination_path = dest_path

>> task.automated = automated

>> task.replace_existing = replace

>> task.save = True

>>

>> unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])

>> return list(task.imported_object_paths or [])

>>

>> def make_master_material(name: str, dest_path: str):

>> ensure_dir(dest_path)

>> pkg = f"{dest_path}/{name}"

>>

>> if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

>> return unreal.load_asset(pkg)

>>

>> mat = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

>> name, dest_path, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew()

>> )

>>

>> mel = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary

>>

>> # BaseColor param

>> base_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 0)

>> base_param.parameter_name = "BaseColorTex"

>>

>> # Normal param

>> norm_param = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -600, 220)

>> norm_param.parameter_name = "NormalTex"

>> norm_param.sampler_type = unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL

>>

>> # Roughness constant (slightly rough by default)

>> rough = mel.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -600, 420)

>> rough.set_editor_property("r", 0.7)

>>

>> mel.connect_material_property(base_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)

>> mel.connect_material_property(norm_param, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)

>> mel.connect_material_property(rough, "R", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)

>>

>> mel.recompile_material(mat)

>> unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

>> return mat

>>

>> def make_material_instance(mi_name: str, parent_mat, dest_path: str):

>> ensure_dir(dest_path)

>> pkg = f"{dest_path}/{mi_name}"

>>

>> if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(pkg):

>> return unreal.load_asset(pkg)

>>

>> mi = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(

>> mi_name, dest_path, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew()

>> )

>> mi.set_editor_property("parent", parent_mat)

>> unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(pkg)

>> return mi

>>

>> def set_mi_texture(mi, param_name: str, tex_asset):

>> unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param_name, tex_asset)

>> unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi)

>>

>> def choose_master_for_name(asset_name_lower: str) -> str:

>> if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in METAL_HINTS):

>> return "Master_Metal"

>> if any(h in asset_name_lower for h in CONCRETE_HINTS):

>> return "Master_Concrete"

>> return "Master_Prison"

>>

>> def guess_texture_role(filename_lower: str) -> str:

>> # crude but effective heuristics

>> if "normal" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_n") or "_n_" in filename_lower or filename_lower.endswith("_nrm"):

>> return "NormalTex"

>> return "BaseColorTex"

>>

>> def assign_materials_to_mesh(mesh_asset, material_asset):

>> if not isinstance(mesh_asset, unreal.StaticMesh):

>> return

>> slots = list(mesh_asset.get_editor_property("static_materials") or [])

>> if not slots:

>> return

>> for i in range(len(slots)):

>> slots[i].material_interface = material_asset

>> mesh_asset.set_editor_property("static_materials", slots)

>> mesh_asset.mark_package_dirty()

>> unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mesh_asset)

>>

>> def fixup_redirectors(root_path: str):

>> asset_tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()

>> redirs = []

>> for a in unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.list_assets(root_path, recursive=True, include_folder=False):

>> obj = unreal.load_asset(a)

>> if isinstance(obj, unreal.ObjectRedirector):

>> redirs.append(obj)

>> if redirs:

>> asset_tools.fixup_redirectors(redirs)

>> log(f"Fixup redirectors: {len(redirs)}")

>> else:

>> log("Fixup redirectors: none")

>>

>> def run():

>> if not os.path.isdir(VAULT_ROOT):

>> err(f"Vault root not found: {VAULT_ROOT}")

>> return

>>

>> ensure_dir(DEST_ROOT)

>> ensure_dir(TEXTURES_DIR)

>> ensure_dir(MESHES_DIR)

>> ensure_dir(MATS_DIR)

>>

>> # Create masters

>> master_prison = make_master_material("Master_Prison", MATS_DIR)

>> master_conc = make_master_material("Master_Concrete", MATS_DIR)

>> master_metal = make_master_material("Master_Metal", MATS_DIR)

>>

>> masters = {

>> "Master_Prison": master_prison,

>> "Master_Concrete": master_conc,

>> "Master_Metal": master_metal,

>> }

>>

>> fbx_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, {".fbx"})

>> png_files = find_files(VAULT_ROOT, {".png"})

>> log(f"Found FBX: {len(fbx_files)} | PNG: {len(png_files)}")

>>

>> # Import textures first (so we can assign them)

>> texture_map = {} # key: folderLower -> {basenameLower: textureAsset}

>> for p in png_files:

>> imported = import_file(p, TEXTURES_DIR)

>> for obj_path in imported:

>> tex = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

>> folder = os.path.dirname(p).lower()

>> base = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0].lower()

>> texture_map.setdefault(folder, {})[base] = tex

>>

>> # Import meshes and wire materials

>> for fbx in fbx_files:

>> base_name = safe_asset_name(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(fbx))[0])

>> imported = import_file(fbx, MESHES_DIR)

>>

>> mesh = None

>> for obj_path in imported:

>> obj = unreal.load_asset(obj_path)

>> if isinstance(obj, unreal.StaticMesh):

>> mesh = obj

>> break

>>

>> if not mesh:

>> warn(f"Skipping (no StaticMesh found): {fbx}")

>> continue

>>

>> master_key = choose_master_for_name(base_name.lower())

>> parent = masters.get(master_key, master_prison)

>>

>> mi = make_material_instance(f"MI_{base_name}", parent, MATS_DIR)

>>

>> folder = os.path.dirname(fbx).lower()

>> candidates = texture_map.get(folder, {})

>>

>> # Apply best guesses: match textures containing the mesh basename

>> for bn, tex in candidates.items():

>> if bn.startswith(base_name.lower()) or base_name.lower() in bn:

>> role = guess_texture_role(bn)

>> set_mi_texture(mi, role, tex)

>>

>> assign_materials_to_mesh(mesh, mi)

>>

>> fixup_redirectors(DEST_ROOT)

>> log("✅ Vault import + material assignment complete.")

>>

>> if __name__ == "__main__":

>> run()

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Source\Nyghtshade\Nyghtshade.Build.cs

>> # ---------------------------

>> $build_cs = @'

>> using UnrealBuildTool;

>> using System;

>> using System.IO;

>>

>> public class Nyghtshade : ModuleRules

>> {

>> public Nyghtshade(ReadOnlyTargetRules Target) : base(Target)

>> {

>> PCHUsage = PCHUsageMode.UseExplicitOrSharedPCHs;

>>

>> PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]

>> {

>> "Core",

>> "CoreUObject",

>> "Engine",

>> "InputCore",

>> "Projects"

>> });

>>

>> PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]

>> {

>> "Slate",

>> "SlateCore"

>> });

>>

>> // Project root: <Project>/Source/Nyghtshade -> <Project>

>> string ProjectRoot = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "..", ".."));

>>

>> // Optional externals at:

>> // <Project>/crown-master

>> // <Project>/IntegratedDynamics

>> string CrownRoot = Path.Combine(ProjectRoot, "crown-master");

>> string DynRoot = Path.Combine(ProjectRoot, "IntegratedDynamics");

>>

>> bool HasCrown = Directory.Exists(CrownRoot);

>> bool HasDyn = Directory.Exists(DynRoot);

>>

>> PublicDefinitions.Add(HasCrown ? "WITH_CROWN=1" : "WITH_CROWN=0");

>> PublicDefinitions.Add(HasDyn ? "WITH_INTEGRATED_DYNAMICS=1" : "WITH_INTEGRATED_DYNAMICS=0");

>>

>> // Add reasonable include roots if they exist (safe even if empty)

>> if (HasCrown)

>> {

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(CrownRoot, "Source"));

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(CrownRoot, "Include"));

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(CrownRoot, "Public"));

>> }

>>

>> if (HasDyn)

>> {

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(DynRoot, "Source"));

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(DynRoot, "Include"));

>> AddIfExists(Path.Combine(DynRoot, "Public"));

>> }

>>

>> // Bridge include path

>> PublicIncludePaths.Add(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "Public"));

>> PublicIncludePaths.Add(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "Public", "Bridge"));

>> PrivateIncludePaths.Add(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "Private"));

>> PrivateIncludePaths.Add(Path.Combine(ModuleDirectory, "Private", "Bridge"));

>> }

>>

>> private void AddIfExists(string PathToAdd)

>> {

>> if (Directory.Exists(PathToAdd))

>> {

>> PublicIncludePaths.Add(PathToAdd);

>> }

>> }

>> }

>> '@

>>

>> # ---------------------------

>> # Bridge shims

>> # ---------------------------

>> $crown_h = @'

>> #pragma once

>>

>> #include "CoreMinimal.h"

>>

>> namespace Nyghtshade

>> {

2. Analysis of the "Buddy Network" Concept

Your idea falls squarely into the domain of Distributed Computing, Grid Computing, and Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks (DePIN), but with a unique focus on peer-to-peer (P2P) resource sharing for creative work like game development.



A. Current Landscape (What Already Exists)

You are absolutely right that renting high-performance computing (HPC) power is common.



Cloud HPC (Commercial): Services like AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure offer powerful GPU instances (NVIDIA A100s, H100s) ideal for AI training and rendering. This is robust but costly.



Grid/Volunteer Computing (Academic/Scientific): Projects like Folding@Home use idle CPU/GPU cycles from millions of volunteers globally for scientific simulations. The key difference: users donate cycles for a single, massive task, not for personalized, interactive development environments.



Decentralized GPU Networks (Emerging): Companies like Akash Network or Render Network (DePIN projects) are building marketplaces where hardware owners rent out their idle GPUs to others, often using blockchain technology for payment and security. This is the closest analog to your "Buddy Network."



B. The Challenge and Novelty of the "Buddy Network"

The main hurdles for your "Buddy Network" idea are Latency and Security/Isolation.



Challenge Existing Solution/Technology Novelty of "Buddy Assist"

Security & Privacy Virtual Machines (VMs), Sandbox environments. The "Firewall" concept is critical. It must guarantee zero access to personal files and processes. This requires a hypervisor or OS-level containerization visible only to the consuming process.

Latency/Transfer High-speed Internet (fiber), Remote Desktop Protocols (RDP), streaming technology. Game development often needs instantaneous feedback (especially for real-time rendering or compiling). A typical consumer internet connection would introduce unacceptable latency for interactive work, making it only suitable for batch jobs (like lightmap baking, video rendering, or CI/CD builds).

Fair Scheduling Centralized schedulers (Kubernetes). Decentralized Scheduling is the hard part. The network needs an intelligent way to assign tasks to the best available idle peer instantly and securely.

C. Technical Feasibility (Can We Make That a Thing?)

Yes, it is theoretically possible, but it is a massive undertaking.



To make the "Buddy Network" a reality for game developers, you would need to build a specialized stack:



Peer-to-Peer Discovery: A system (perhaps using a decentralized ledger or a simple P2P overlay) to let idle PCs ("Buddies") advertise their spare CPU/GPU cycles.



Secure Sandboxing: A lightweight hypervisor or container (like Docker/Podman, but simpler for consumer use) that spins up a completely isolated execution environment on the "Buddy's" hardware when they enable "Buddy Assist." This is the firewall protection you mentioned.



Image of a decentralized compute network architecture

Shutterstock

Task Streamer/Splitter: A client-side application (which could be integrated into your existing Gemini Console!) that takes a heavy task (e.g., building a complex Shader Graph, baking a NavMesh) and automatically breaks it down into small, transmissible tasks that are sent to multiple "Buddies" for parallel processing.



Low-Latency Sync (Optional): For actual interactive work (not just batch processing), you would need ultra-low latency streaming, similar to what cloud gaming services (like GeForce Now or Stadia/Luna) use, which is difficult over heterogeneous residential networks.



Your concept moves beyond simple cloud rental and introduces a powerful community resource model, specifically addressing the cost and accessibility barriers for indie game developers. It's a great vision for a potential DePIN startup focused on creative cloud computing!

Hardware specs



Current load



Latency



Past reliability



Nodes receive tasks and execute in sandbox.



Result Collection



Tasks return to Aggregator.



Results verified via checksum / redundancy (duplicate tasks on multiple nodes for reliability).

# Logic for the Buddy_Monitor.py
import time
from pynput import mouse, keyboard

class BuddyMonitor:
    def __init__(self):
        self.last_activity = time.time()
        self.is_buddy_active = False

    def on_activity(self, *args):
        self.last_activity = time.time()
        if self.is_buddy_active:
            self.kill_all_tasks()

    def run(self):
        while True:
            idle_time = time.time() - self.last_activity
            if idle_time > 600: # 10 Minutes
                self.start_buddy_assist()
            time.sleep(10)

2. The Idle Sentry & Screensaver Script
This Python script stays in the background. It watches the clock and the mouse. At the 10-minute mark, it locks the PC into "Buddy Mode" and displays your custom image.

File: Buddy_Sentry.py

Python
import time
import sys
import os
from pynput import mouse, keyboard
import tkinter as tk # For the full-screen image overlay

class EqualAccessSentry:
    def __init__(self, image_path):
        self.idle_limit = 600  # 10 minutes in seconds
        self.last_activity = time.time()
        self.is_pulling = False
        self.image_path = image_path
        self.root = None

    def reset_timer(self, *args):
        self.last_activity = time.time()
        if self.is_pulling:
            self.stop_screensaver()

    def start_screensaver(self):
        self.is_pulling = True
        print("[THE FORGE] PC Idle. Buddy Network Pull: ACTIVE.")
        
        # Create a full-screen window with your image
        self.root = tk.Tk()
        self.root.attributes("-fullscreen", True)
        self.root.configure(bg='black')
        
        # Load your "Forge Active" Image
        img = tk.PhotoImage(file=self.image_path)
        label = tk.Label(self.root, image=img, bg='black')
        label.pack(expand=True)
        
        # Text Overlay
        info = tk.Label(self.root, text="FORGE ACTIVE: Hardware assisting the network.\nMove mouse to resume.", 
                         fg="cyan", bg="black", font=("Arial", 20))
        info.pack(side="bottom", pady=50)
        
        self.root.mainloop()

    def stop_screensaver(self):
        self.is_pulling = False
        if self.root:
            self.root.destroy()
            self.root = None
        print("[THE FORGE] Activity detected. Buddy Network Pull: KILLED.")

    def run(self):
        # Listen for any key or mouse movement
        m_listener = mouse.Listener(on_move=self.reset_timer, on_click=self.reset_timer)
        k_listener = keyboard.Listener(on_press=self.reset_timer)
        m_listener.start()
        k_listener.start()

        while True:
            if not self.is_pulling:
                idle_duration = time.time() - self.last_activity
                if idle_duration > self.idle_limit:
                    self.start_screensaver()
            time.sleep(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Point this to your image file
    sentry = EqualAccessSentry("The_Forge_Active.png")
    sentry.run()

1. How Task Splitting Works (The Logic)
